relations.note: The canonical enumeration places the eight principal Ajogun under Èṣù’s operative command.
relations.source: Ifá verse quoted in Emory dissertation

relations.note: Èṣù conveys correctly performed offerings and redirects the Ajogun away from their intended victim.
Ọ̀rúnmìlà detects threatened misfortune and prescribes sacrifice, medicine, correction, or ritual deception.
Modern accounts describe the Ajogun obstructing destiny, while sacrifice and good character preserve alignment with Orí.

relations.myth: Creation of forces for cosmic regulation
relations.note: Some contemporary teachers say Olódùmarè established the Ajogun as regulatory forces; no early creation text was verified.
Ikú, Death, precedes or commands the other Ajogun as their foremost and gravest member.
Àrùn, Disease, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Òfò, Loss, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Ẹ̀gbà, Paralysis, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Ọ̀ràn, Great Trouble, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Èpè, Curse, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Ẹ̀wọ̀n, Imprisonment, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Èṣe, Affliction, appears as a principal co-member in the canonical enumeration and concerted assaults.
Some Ifá verses describe witches as deploying Ajogun, although the two adversarial classes remain distinct.
